it’s all over! phrase

also it’s over, it’s all up, that’s the end of me, it’s all over with me, all is lost, we’re done for, that’s the end, game over, when the battle was over

classical

Plaut. Cist. 4.2.17: āctumst; īlicet mē īnfēlīcem (Lewis & Short s.v. agō)
Traupman 92
Ter. Ad. 324: Periimus: āctum est.
Plaut. Trin. 3.4.194: āctum est dē collō meō (Lewis & Short s.v. agō)
Traupman 105: it’s all over!, āctum est! or īlicet!

Āctum est!

impersonal perfect passive of agō; with dē + abl., it’s all up with

it’s all over! it’s finished

The perfect passive of agere, “it has been done”: nothing more can be done about it.

Other words

  • āctum est dē (+ abl.) — it’s all over with (someone or something)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 1.1.63: āctum hodiē est dē mē; Liv. 1.47 (Lewis & Short s.v. agō); Traupman 97; Traupman 309

    “That’s the end of me” is āctum est dē mē.

  • Īlicet! — it’s all over! that’s the end!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Cist. 4.2.17: āctumst; īlicet mē īnfēlīcem (Lewis & Short s.v. agō); Traupman 105: it’s all over!, īlicet! · Wiktionary

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    From īre licet, “you may go”, the formula that dismissed an assembly when its business was over (Lewis & Short); hence “it’s finished”. Not to be confused with īlicō, on the spot.

Examples

  • āctumst; īlicet mē īnfēlīcem

    it’s all over; it’s finished, poor mePlaut. Cist. 4.2.17 (Lewis & Short)

  • āctum hodiē est dē mē

    it’s all over with me todayPlaut. Ps. 1.1.63 (Lewis & Short)

  • jam dē Serviō āctum

    by now it was all over with ServiusLiv. 1.47 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quid est? quid trepidās? … — Periimus: āctum est.

    What is it? Why the panic? … — We’re done for: it’s all over.Ter. Ad. 323–325

  • cōnfectō proeliō

    when the battle was overTraupman 355

See also I’m done for!, never mind.
